logline: Florence, 1504. Leonardo builds a machine meant to translate his ideas. Instead it starts transmitting, and someone in the future is listening.
tagline: A message from the past, asking the future to help it happen.

voice.name: Old Italian Man angry and nostalgic
voice.direction: played dry; muffled whenever he speaks from the next room

cast.role: music, D minor, 92 BPM; the machine's tenor voice sings

scenes.title: The impossible expense
scenes.summary: Leonardo totals forty-seven florins; Agnolo arrives with the ledger and books the plan under "losses."
scenes.question: Who pays for a machine that talks to people who haven't been born yet?

scenes.title: The Unspoken Orchestra
scenes.summary: The machine sings what Leonardo won't say: he is terrified of dying with a thousand unfinished ideas.
scenes.question: What is the inventor really afraid of?

scenes.title: The first broadcast
scenes.summary: The machine isn't translating, it's sending. A listener in the future: "leave it on. I like this one."
scenes.question: Is anyone there?

scenes.title: The pitch across centuries
scenes.summary: Leonardo asks the future for help; the machine turns his explanation into "Make It With Me" (3:56). The needle counts who is listening.
scenes.question: What if we could help one another finish them?

scenes.title: A voice from the library
scenes.summary: Borges answers from the library, names the radio, and asks whether the future is already listening.
scenes.question: Has the future already been listening?

scenes.title: The bill
scenes.summary: Agnolo turns the month into a $3,000 bill and predicts the second transmission costs twenty (8:20). Leonardo asks the listener for help paying for the time it took to find them.
scenes.question: Does anyone value it enough to pay for the time it took to make?

ideas.title: Episode 001: The First Transmission
ideas.question: Can a complete eight-minute audio pilot prove the machine works, and ask the future for help without feeling like a donation request?
ideas.reason: The pilot: produce the audio first, release it, then see whether it raises enough to make the next one.
ideas.result: Released as a 9:00 audio-first episode with a robot-portrait video for YouTube. 76 scripted lines, verified by transcribing the final mix.

ideas.title: Agnolo's Ledger: the real numbers, spoken in the fiction
ideas.question: Can each episode report its real production cost inside the story?
ideas.reason: Cut into E01 scene 6 so the $3,000-versus-$20 prediction is public before Episode 002 is made; recurs from Episode 002 as a postscript reporting each episode's real cost against the prediction.

ideas.title: Robot-portrait video broadcast
ideas.question: Can a static design with waveforms in robot mouths carry an audio episode on YouTube, and become a running gag?
ideas.reason: Chosen over plain colour-coded waveforms: funnier, and a callback for later episodes.
ideas.result: 1920×1080 video of the episode with robot portraits of Leonardo, Agnolo and Borges; thumbnail made.

ideas.title: Orchestra escalation cues for scene 2
ideas.question: Should two new cues build the orchestra's escalation in scene 2?
ideas.reason: The two new cues didn't build clearly; the escalation uses the Not Enough Time lute intro, the sad-violin stinger, then the chorus. Cost $0.28.

ideas.title: OpenHome ability: link delivery and subscriptions
ideas.question: Can the device send the contribution link and subscribe listeners to the next transmission?
ideas.reason: OpenHome ability work deferred to later; the device outro is scripted but not built.

decisions: Agnolo's voice is the stock "Old Italian Man" library voice, directed to sound dry, muffled whenever he speaks from the next room.
Scene 2's escalation: the Not Enough Time lute intro, then the sad-violin stinger, then a swell into the real chorus. Two new escalation cues were left out.
"Make It With Me" is take 2, matching the overture's tempo and key. Takes 1 and 4 also have every word right.

Agnolo's Ledger was cut into scene 6, right after "Then we will have learned something expensive" and before Leonardo's final address, so the $3,000-versus-$20 contrast lands just before he asks the listener for help.
Money framing: contributions pay back Episode 001's artist time (30 days at $100 a day). They do not buy Episode 002, and they are not refundable.
Scene 4: the line saying the needle funds the next transmission was cut; it contradicted that framing.
Audio first. Visual styles come later; the video uses robot portraits with waveforms in their mouths.

leonardo: Transmits from Florence, in the year 1504.
Built the machine to say what he means when his words are too slow; it has opinions and insists on singing, in a voice better than his.
Is terrified he will die with a thousand unfinished ideas: wings, bridges, a city with streets on two levels, a face he has been painting for four years.
Keeps a cat he calls a research cat; the beeswax was her idea.
Named the radio "Future radio" after Borges said the word.
agnolo: Messer Agnolo is Leonardo's bookkeeper, usually heard from the next room, with a quill and an abacus.
Books what he can't invoice under "losses"; entered the cat's fish under "research."
Billed the first transmission at three thousand dollars — thirty days of Leonardo's life — and predicted the second costs twenty, "if your calculations are correct."
borges: An unfortunate reader in a library that is rather difficult to explain.
Has been hearing Leonardo's broadcasts for a long time, in fragments between the shelves — though Episode 001 is the first one.
Gave the radio its name: he has been waiting for someone to invent it.

release.invitation: The transmission is yours: hear it, share it, enjoy it. If you'd like there to be more of them, help pay back the time it took to find you. Contributions aren't refundable; progress is posted on Twitter.
